u3Rate.unit: % of civilian labor force, official unemployment rate (U-3), seasonally adjusted
u3Rate.source: BLS Employment Situation, October 2026, published 2026-11-06, Table A-1 and A-15; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_11062026.htm (re-read 2026-11-12)

unemployed.unit: million people unemployed, seasonally adjusted (shown rounded as 7.1M)
unemployed.source: BLS Employment Situation, Table A-1, published 2026-11-06 (re-read 2026-11-12)

laborForce.unit: million, civilian labor force, seasonally adjusted (shown rounded as 170.7M)
laborForce.source: BLS Employment Situation, Table A-1, published 2026-11-06 (re-read 2026-11-12)

u3Check.unit: % computed in code: 7.068 / 170.683 (scenes/math.ts); rounds to the published 4.1%
u3Check.source: Computed from BLS Table A-1 levels

u6Rate.unit: % U-6: unemployed + all marginally attached + part-time for economic reasons, as % of labor force + marginally attached, seasonally adjusted
u6Rate.source: BLS Employment Situation, Table A-15, published 2026-11-06 (re-read 2026-11-12)

partTimeEconomic.unit: million, part-time for economic reasons, seasonally adjusted

definition.value: No job in the reference week, available for work, actively looked in the prior 4 weeks (or on temporary layoff)
definition.source: BLS CPS Concepts & Definitions, https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm (page modified 2026-11-03)

notes: Household survey (CPS) figures, seasonally adjusted, subject to annual revision.
U-6 adds all 'marginally attached' workers (discouraged workers are a subset) plus part-time for economic reasons; S4 wording 'want work but stopped looking' covers the marginally attached group.

The S4 stacked bar shows only the published 4.1% and 7.9% endpoints; the added band is not split into sized layers because BLS does not publish each layer as a share of the U-6 denominator in this release.
Discouraged workers (448K SA) are in the key facts only, not on screen.
